verdict_reason: The kernel is untouched this round and remains the released IsoScore: _isoscore vs the installed IsoScore 2.0.1 package gives 0.9667461859774082 vs 0.9667461841527681 on an isotropic 2000x64 Gaussian (rel 1.89e-09), rel 2.64e-07 on a rank-8-in-R^64 cloud and 1.52e-05 under extreme anisotropy (where BLME is the MORE accurate of the two, because the official route squares the data into torch.cov before the SVD). The algebra matches Rudman et al. Eq. 4.1 term for term. This round's change is CONFIG only (study num_samples 200 -> 1000) and it does what it claims on gpt2: driving the real evaluate(), _meta_points_per_dim goes 30.30 -> 175.19 and _meta_sampling_regime_ok goes False -> True, with isoscore 0.000659629 -> 0.000791527 (+20.0%), reproducing the recorded figure exactly. The decision NOT to NaN-gate on the ratio also remains correct, and I re-derived why: at 1000 documents the corpus yields 134,543 gpt2 tokens, so points_per_dim = 134543/d clears the declared 50 only for d_model <= 2690 -- gating would still discard every model wider than that, i.e. most of the zoo's large end, to avoid a bias I measure at well under a percent on real states.
comparable_reason: Raw isoscore carries a structural 1/(d-1) factor: rho -0.433 with d_model (p=2.8e-04) and -0.463 with log-params over the 66-model archive, and a zero-padding isometry that leaves the cloud unchanged moves the raw score 0.110955 -> 0.027412 -> 0.006833 -> 0.001707 at d = 64/256/1024/4096, a factor of 65 from ambient dimension alone. The config change does not touch this. It ALSO introduces a second, new comparability problem: the finite-N regime is now model-dependent in a way it was not, because at a fixed 1000 documents points_per_dim = 134543/d falls from 175 (d=768) to 26 (d=5120) to 19 (d=7168).
github_reason: The official package is installed on this host. I read IsoScore.IsoScore's source (torch.cov -> svdvals -> pcs*sqrt(n)/||pcs|| -> defect -> rescale) and ran it head-to-head against _isoscore on four clouds; worst relative disagreement 1.52e-05, on the case where the official's cov-then-SVD route loses precision. BLME's only deliberate departures are the float64 promotion, the S/S[0] rescale (both exactly cancelling) and a [0,1] clamp the reference lacks.
paper_reason: Rudman et al.'s defining anchors reproduce: an isotropic Gaussian at n >> d scores 0.9667 against the paper's -> 1 limit (the finite-N floor at this (n,d) is 0.9668, so the value sits AT the floor), and a k-dimensional cloud embedded in d ambient dimensions scores (k/d - 1/d)/(1 - 1/d) -- 0.110955 at d=64 against the closed form 0.111111 (0.14%) and 0.0017070 at d=4096 against 0.00170898 (0.11%).
confounds_reason: Raw isoscore rho -0.433 with d_model (p=2.8e-04), -0.310 with n_layers, -0.463 with log-params over 66 models; the zero-padding isometry shows the association is the structural 1/(d-1) factor. isoscore_effective_dims removes it (rho -0.089, p=0.48) and is invariant under the same isometry to 8.4e-15 (7.990170056143993 at d=64 and 7.9901700561439215 at d=4096).
defects: 1000 IS NOT ENOUGH, AND WHETHER IT IS ENOUGH DEPENDS ON THE MODEL. Driving the real evaluate() at N = 200 / 1000 / 2000 documents: gpt2 isoscore 0.000659629 / 0.000791527 / 0.000794920 -- +20.0% then +0.43%, so gpt2 has converged by 1000. pythia-160m, the SAME width (768) and the same 177 points per dimension, gives 0.139130920 / 0.064517918 / 0.089038856 -- -53.6% then **+38.0%**, and it is not even monotone (isoscore_effective_dims 107.71 -> 50.49 -> 69.29). A 38% move between 1000 and 2000 documents on one of the two models tested means the shipped 1000 does not pin the value, and the residual bias is model-dependent, which is exactly the property that made 200 unusable.

THE CONFIG CHANGE SILENTLY BROKE `_meta_isoscore_null_floor`, the field that exists so a reader can judge the sampling regime. _isoscore_null_floor caps the synthetic draw at 40M cells, and its docstring says the subsample 'carries the same bias' because it holds N/d fixed -- it does not; it holds N*d fixed and therefore CHANGES N/d. At 200 documents (N=23,272, 17.9M cells) the cap did not bind and the reported floor was exact. At the new 1000 it does: reported 0.985425757 against the true floor at (134543, 768) of 0.994294470, understating it by -0.892%; at 2000 documents reported 0.985425757 against a true 0.996808505, -1.142%. Both N=1000 and N=2000 report the IDENTICAL floor, which is the fingerprint. Immaterial for gpt2 (whose isoscore is 1000x below the floor) but the field is now wrong precisely in the regime the change created.

CONFIG, still open at the wide end: at 1000 documents the realized supply is 134,543 tokens (gpt2 tokenizer, 512-token window), so _meta_sampling_regime_ok is False for every model with d_model > 2690 -- measured points_per_dim 32.8 at d=4096, 26.3 at 5120, 25.0 at 5376, 18.8 at 7168, all under the declared min_points_per_dim: 50. Models with larger vocabularies produce FEWER tokens for the same corpus, so the real figure for Llama/Qwen-class checkpoints is worse than this.

ARCHIVE INCOMPATIBILITY, not recorded as such in the study config's note: the value moves by a MODEL-DEPENDENT amount between the old and new settings (gpt2 +20.0%, pythia-160m -53.6%), so archived isoscore values cannot be pooled with new ones, and the difference is not a common offset.

defaults.yaml's own comment for this task still says 'the value is NaN-gated below it rather than silently emitted' (line 24-25). The code deliberately does NOT gate -- there is a 20-line comment saying so 400 lines away. The config file documents behaviour the code was changed to stop having.

The undersized-cache refusal reads the private attribute cache._sample_lengths via getattr with a [] default, so a cache refactor silently makes the guard vacuous (same pattern as geometry_magnitude and geometry_vendi_score).

isoscore_effective_dims IS the covariance participation ratio (verified: iso*(d-1)+1 equals (sum lam)^2/sum(lam^2) to rel 0.0 / 7.8e-16 / 2.2e-16 on three clouds), which geometry_svd already emits as participation_ratio. The two must not both enter a feature matrix.
